National Tradesmen Day is an annual observance in the United States dedicated
to recognizing and celebrating the vital work done by tradespeople-such as carpenters, electricians, plumbers, masons, mechanics, HVAC technicians, and other skilled workers in the construction and maintenance
industries.
The day aims to spotlight the essential role tradesmen and tradeswomen play in building, maintaining, and improving homes, schools, hospitals, roads, businesses, and critical infrastructure. It also seeks to show appreciation for their hard work, expertise, and the value they bring to communities and the country as a whole.
National Tradesmen Day was established by Irwin Tools in 2011 as a way to thank tradesmen for their important contributions.
National Tradesmen Day is celebrated on the third Friday in September each year. In 2024, it falls on September 20th.
How is it observed?
• Employers, contractors, and communities often take the day to thank their teams, provide special meals, distribute gifts, or offer public recognition.
• Education campaigns may highlight the importance of trades careers, addressing skilled labor shortages and encouraging young people to consider the trades.
• Social media campaigns and local media often feature stories about outstanding tradesmen.
